penetration_assumption: Every rupee below is ESTIMATED and anchored on ARY's OWN comparable lines, not on the research fleet's bands. (1) Prep bench Rs 1,12,000: ARY writes 87 fruit bills a day (30,924 fruit bills / 354 trading days, VERIFIED); assume ONE prepared pack per 20 fruit bills = ~4.4 packs/day at Rs 70 = Rs 1.12 L/yr at 30% (yield loss + labour, above the 12.7% whole-fruit rate). Deliberately conservative because these 4 SKUs are ALREADY listed and sold Rs 200 in their lifetime. (2) Hampers Rs 62,400: 2 baskets/week at Rs 600 for hospital visits, Gurpurab and convocation, 25% assembly margin. (3) Kimia dates Rs 20,000: matches ARY's existing DRY-date turnover of Rs 21,078. (4) Persimmon Rs 15,000: one 6-week Nov-Dec window, sized at ARY's best exotic (Blue Berry Rs 16,520). (5) Avocado Rs 13,000 and (6) pomelo Rs 10,000: the median/floor of ARY's four existing exotics — Dragon Fruit Rs 14,735, Blue Berry Rs 16,520, Cherry Rs 12,810, Strawberry Rs 6,613. A NEW exotic has no reason to beat the ones already on the rack. (7) Frozen pulp Rs 15,000: one slow packaged line at 20%. SEPARATE AND LARGER: the availability prize on the EXISTING range. Fruit share of store sales runs 2.35-2.83% in Oct-Dec while the campus is FULL (29-33k bills/month), against 4.22% in April. Holding Oct-Dec at merely the April share on the same store turnover = +Rs 3,07,534/yr, no new SKU, no new supplier, no licence — more than everything on the add-list above.
probe_evidence: The coverage diff is unreliable in BOTH directions and I re-tested every line. Its ONE "missing" verdict is a FALSE MISS: `ary assort probe chiku` returns 2 SKUs, 1 selling — 07OH "Chiku", Rs 20,456 over 136 selling days at Rs 74.31/kg avg, last sale 2026-08-16. ARY simply spells it Chiku, not chikoo/sapota (probe on chikoo=0, sapota=0). The more dangerous errors are the FALSE COVEREDs, all caused by broad single-word matching: "Avocado — covered, 10 SKUs, Rs 10,922" → probe shows all 10 live in Personal Care (Bath Soap 5, Body Wash Gel 1, Shower Gel 3) + Toiletories 1. "Grapefruit/pomelo — covered, 430 SKUs, Rs 4.95 L" matched the word 'fruit'; probe grapefruit = 3 SKUs, all Bath Soap/Shower Gel; pomelo = 0; chakotra = 0. "Strawberry — covered, Rs 5,55,758" matched 'winter' (Winter Wear jackets); real fresh strawberry = one SKU, Rs 6,613, 15 selling days. "Muskmelon/Sarda — covered, Rs 4,90,516" matched 'sarda' (Sardar Blazer); the two real Sarda SKUs — Melon(Shrda) and Sharda Fruit — have ZERO 12m sales and last sold in 2024. "Amla — covered, Rs 1,51,271" matched hair oil and shampoo; real fresh amla = one SKU in the VEGETABLE group, Rs 10,918. "Fresh soft dates — covered" matched 'soft'; probe kimia=0, mazafati=0 (only dry dates, Rs 21,078). "Frozen fruit — covered" matched 'mango'; the Frozen group is McCain potato products + paneer + peas, zero fruit. "Cut fruit bowl / arils / hamper — covered, Rs 4.95 L" all matched 'fruit'; probe "fruit salad" = 4 SKUs in Others with ZERO 12m sales (lifetime: Fruit Salad Large sold TWICE, Rs 200, last 2023-07-02; the other three have NEVER sold a unit), probe hamper = 0, no arils SKU exists. Institutional bulk (a "must-have") is ALREADY covered: the _Z SKUs are one account, Hunger Heroes, 12 bills, Rs 3,18,434/yr out of the Basement warehouse.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but the assortment premise is wrong and the verdict is AVAILABILITY, proven three ways. (1) BREADTH IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT — VERIFIED: 55 fruit SKUs sold in the live 12m window, plus ~199 inactive legacy "Fruits <name> 2xxx" listings and several active-never-sold duplicates (Lychee 0 lifetime while Litchi Fruit does Rs 30,860; Gooseberry 0 while Amla sells; Pineapple 0 while Pine Apple Rani does Rs 23,463). ARY lists the range and does not keep it on the shelf. (2) CONTINUITY IS THE CONSTRAINT — VERIFIED from the purchase ledger: 98% of fruit purchases (Rs 31,38,819 of Rs 32.0 L) come from ONE agent, M/S Shashi Bhushan Manoj Kumar Aeron, delivering on 132 of 365 days; fruit deliveries fall to 10-13 days a month in Oct-Dec. Even the No.1 line, Apple Improted, records a sale on only 274 of 354 trading days; Banana Kg on 168 of 354. Fruit-line breadth halves in the peak domestic season (25 SKUs in Oct, 24 in Nov, 27 in Dec vs 44 in May), and fruit's share of store sales bottoms at 2.35% in December while the campus is at full strength. CONFOUND I MUST NAME: January's collapse is NOT fruit-specific — whole-store bills fall to 15,078 from 41,388 in May, so January is a campus-empty month (winter break), not a supply failure. The Oct-Dec anomaly survives that control; January does not. That is why confidence is medium, not high. (3) MARGIN KILLS THE ADD-SKUS CASE — VERIFIED from PurchaseDetail.ItemValue vs SaleDetail.FinalSaleAmount, same 12m window, NOT the price master (which Trap 4 says is biased high): fruit purchases Rs 30,05,727 against fruit sales Rs 34,44,737 = Rs 4,39,010 realised gross margin = 12.7%, against 27.0% store-wide (Rs 5.60 Cr purchases vs Rs 7.67 Cr sales). GST on fruit is Rs 0 and 12m fruit returns are Rs 85, so gross is net. Per-SKU, EVERY line lands 10.1-17.4%: Dragon Fruit 11.0%, Blue Berry 11.9%, Cherry 10.6%, Strawberry 13.4%, Jamun 10.1%, Kiwi 17.3%, Apple Improted 17.4%. The demand research's "30-45% gross on exotics" is not achievable here — ARY earns 11% on dragon fruit. Adding fruit SKUs at 12.7% is the worst rupee in this store. The whole absent+dormant set is Rs 2.47 L of revenue = 0.32% of a Rs 7.67 Cr business, and Rs 60,210 of gross margin — less than the Rs 3.08 L of revenue sitting in Oct-Dec availability on SKUs ARY already lists.
blockers: MARGIN, not licence or capital, is the binding constraint. VERIFIED 12.7% realised gross on fresh fruit vs 27.0% store-wide; every one of 14 fruit SKUs costed off the purchase ledger lands between 10.1% and 17.4%. Any plan that assumes the research corpus's 30-45% exotic margins is wrong before it starts.

SINGLE SUPPLIER. M/S Shashi Bhushan Manoj Kumar Aeron supplies 98% of fruit (Rs 31.39 L of Rs 32.0 L) on 132 of 365 days. No second quote exists anywhere in the ledger — the likeliest cause of the thin margin, and every new line depends on that one agent agreeing to carry it.

NO COLD CHAIN FOR FRUIT. The only freezer evidence is the Frozen group (McCain + paneer + peas). Arils, cut fruit and avocado all need 4C display; that is capex plus power continuity on a hill campus, and it is unbudgeted.

FSSAI SCOPE — NOT CHECKED. Cut fruit, arils and hampers are food handling/manufacturing, needing a prep bench, date labelling and licence cover. I could not verify from the database whether ARY's registration extends to it. This must be checked before any prep-bench spend.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH. Avocado, pomelo, Kimia dates and frozen berries are Azadpur/Chandigarh lines 150-200 km out. The one agent runs a Solan/Paonta circuit; a weekly Azadpur indent is a new logistics leg for Rs 58,000/yr of combined revenue — likely not worth the run on its own.

SHRINK IS NOT MEASURED. The 'Damage (F&V)' account booked Rs 6,280 in 12 months = 0.18% of fruit sales, against an industry 8-15% on fresh. Either wastage is real and invisible, or it is absorbed in unrecorded markdowns. The 30% prep-bench margin assumption rests on knowing this and ARY does not.

THE CUT-FRUIT SKUS ALREADY EXIST AND HAVE NEVER MOVED. 06MQ/06MR/06MS/06MV have Rs 200 of lifetime sales since 2023. I cannot tell from the data whether they were never made or tried and failed. That single unknown is the largest risk in the Rs 1.12 L line, which is 45% of the total sizing.
SHELF. All 53 selling fruit SKUs share one counter ('Fruits & Vegetables' warehouse). Seven new exotics compete for the same rack in the season the staples need it.
CAPITAL IS NOT A BLOCKER — Rs 2.47 L of annual revenue at ~2.5 turns is under Rs 1 L of working capital. Do not let a capital case be built for this; the constraint is margin and continuity.
